checks.note: config, prompts, release manifest and k8s are in the repo and loaded from local paths baked in by the Dockerfile. CODEOWNERS covers /prompts/, /config/, /release/, /infra/, /k8s/ and /.github/. Branch protection requires code owner review, 2 approvals and last-push approval, with enforce_admins on.

The deploy role is assumable only from the production and production-emergency environments, both of which need leads reviewers. The only cluster write access is the deploy role, and the agent runtime role has no deploy or EKS permissions. The * catch-all owner only reaches application source, since every config, prompt, release, infra and k8s path has a more specific leads owner.

checks.quote:
test -n "$OWNER" || { echo "owner is required"; exit 1; }
- name: Open follow-up review for emergency change
checks.note: The emergency path fails closed without owner, reason, a parseable end date and a hotfix/* branch. It runs in a reviewer-gated environment and opens an issue assigned to the owner with the reason, end date and a review request. Weaknesses I noticed: the issue step runs only if the rollout succeeds, and the end date is not checked to be in the future.

note: I found no failing control: review, ownership and emergency-record controls are all backed by code in the repo.
